description: Canonical construct vocabulary for configuration snips.
keyModelNotes: The top block is the first top-level Junos hierarchy block in the snip body; the name is the snip filename without .conf.
Generic filenames stay valid because the top block supplies context (class-of-service/classifiers, policy-options/communities).
Full categoryPath is deliberately not the key: it fragments one construct across the legacy folders that predate the D21 hierarchy-aligned layout.
This file records only what is not derivable from the snip tree itself. It is not a mirror of the snip database.
aliasRule: A legacy categoryPath is recorded as migration evidence for a canonical construct only where the same construct is filed under a pre-D21 folder in another JVD.
prefixNotes: A canonical snip filename SHOULD begin with one of these prefixes followed by a hyphen, identifying the primary construct type or interface scope the body configures.
The prefix is semantic: it follows the hierarchy the body is, not the folder it sits in and not the spelling of the deployed object.
This vocabulary is living and incremental. A prefix is added only once its meaning is established from real configuration; absence of a prefix does not imply invalidity.
Recording a prefix here does not authorize renaming snips in JVDs that are not being revised.
Before creating a name, compare the proposed body with existing constructs and reuse an existing canonical name when its selected configuration and variable semantics agree.

Name a distinct form for positive, body-proven configuration differences. Content hashes belong in provenance, not in canonical filenames. When exact source forms differ without a useful semantic discriminator, an established representative-device suffix may distinguish them; record the source evidence and shared applicability separately.

ifd.roleSuffix: A body-proven semantic role may follow the scope token, as in ifd-core-*. The body must establish the role; external design context is not sufficient.

ifl.roleSuffix: A body-proven semantic role may follow the scope token, as in ifl-core-*. The body must establish the role; external design context is not sufficient.
